sections.html:
Muncie, about 50 miles northeast of Indianapolis, is both the seat and the largest city of Delaware County in east central Indiana. The 2020 census counted 111,903 people in the county and 65,194 in Muncie. A lot of the housing stock is older, so inspectors pay close attention to roofs, gutters and furnaces.

The local economy has moved away from factories toward education, health care and retail. Ball State University and IU Health Ball Memorial Hospital are the largest employers. Growth has gathered on Muncie's north side, while the older industrial south side has seen less. The city reaches across Center, Hamilton, Harrison, Liberty and Mount Pleasant townships, and the Assessor's Office keeps property cards that carry some transfer history.

Demand is shaped by the university. Ball State employed 3,379 people in 2022, IU Health Ball Memorial Hospital 2,613, and Muncie Community Schools 650, so many buyers are staff, faculty and medical workers, and a lot of landlords rent to students. Muncie's population peaked at 76,460 in 1980 and sat at 65,194 in 2020, and the county fell 4.9% over the last decade. Prices are therefore more sensitive to condition than in a fast-growing county. Interstate 69 runs just west of the city, and a house within easy reach of it, or of the Cardinal Greenway rail trail, tends to show well.

Most questions land at the courthouse complex at 100 West Main Street in Muncie. The Auditor's phone is 765-747-7717, and hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

Delaware County tax tasks and where to handle them
TaskOfficeNotes
Change the mailing address on a tax statementAuditor, Room 103In person or by phone at 765-747-7717
Statements not arriving in your namePlat RoomSame phone number
Mortgage deductionAuditor, Room 103Signatures required, so visit in person; a reverse mortgage can qualify with a lender statement showing the debt
Pay or ask about a balanceTreasurer, Room 102100 W Main St
Tax sale surplus questionsAuditor765-747-7717

Not sure which window to walk up to? Start with the Auditor, whose staff can point you to the Treasurer or the Plat Room. Bring your latest tax statement, a photo ID, and for a mortgage deduction the signed forms and your loan papers. A short visit before you list can turn up a wrong name, a missing deduction or an old address on the parcel record, all of which are far cheaper to fix before an offer is in hand than during the closing week.

Payments are due on or before May 10 and November 10. Holiday or weekend dates slide to the next business day. A bill paid within 30 days after the due date, on a parcel with no earlier delinquency, carries a 5% penalty. Every other late bill carries 10%.

Check the name and address on your statement before you list. If the statement goes to an old address, a missed notice becomes a penalty that comes out of your sale proceeds.

Form 130 starts a challenge, and each parcel needs its own. Turn it in by June 15, counting from the year the county mails the assessment notice, or from the year the bill goes out if no notice was sent.

The assessor meets with you informally and passes the outcome to the Property Tax Assessment Board of Appeals. A hearing must follow within 180 days of filing, with notice at least 30 days ahead. If you still disagree, take it to the Indiana Board of Tax Review on Form 131.

Evidence that works: a recent appraisal, sales of similar nearby houses, and photos or estimates for repairs. Start at the Assessor's office with the property card, because a wrong square footage or a structure that was torn down is the easiest error to fix.

A homestead deduction can shrink a bill as much as a lower valuation does. The standard deduction has been 60% of assessed value, up to $48,000, filed by January 5. The rule was amended effective January 1, 2025, so confirm today's numbers with the Auditor.

The deduction does not travel with the house. The new owner has to claim it, and a rental or an empty home can fall into a higher class, so do not promise a buyer that your current bill will carry over.

If a Delaware County parcel sells at a tax sale and the price exceeds what was owed, the extra money is surplus. Only the owner whose property was sold can collect it. Anyone else, including an agent with a power of attorney, has to petition the court.

Surplus is released only after the court issues a tax deed and the deed is recorded at the Delaware County Recorder's Office. Call the Auditor at 765-747-7717 with questions.

Selling before the sale keeps the house out of a certificate holder's hands and stops added costs.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes or other issues
sections.html:
Older houses, inherited property and rental units make up many Delaware County sales. Indiana's sales disclosure form has to be finished before the deed reaches the auditor, with a separate form for each parcel.

  • Get a payoff figure for taxes and penalties.
  • Confirm the mailing address on the tax bill.
  • Gather estate papers if the owner has died.
  • Decide whether repairs pay off before you list.

Cash buyers skip the lender appraisal, and the title company settles taxes out of your proceeds.

In practice, call the Auditor to confirm the balance, make sure statements are reaching you, and tell the title company early about any reverse mortgage or other lien. A seller with several rental parcels should hand the closing agent the full list on day one, since each needs its own disclosure form.

If the owner has died, bring the estate papers and deed history. The Assessor's property card shows some transfers, which lets a title company see whether names line up before the sale record is filed.

Plan the last week carefully. Request an updated payoff right before signing, because a penalty that posted after your first call changes the figure. Keep the receipts for any installment you paid this year, and give the buyer's side a copy of the latest bill so the proration at the table matches what you actually owe.

faqs.q: When are Delaware County property taxes due?
faqs.a: On or before May 10 and November 10 each year, and the date shifts when it falls on a weekend or holiday.

faqs.q: Where do I change the mailing address on my Delaware County tax bill?
faqs.a: At the Auditor's office, 100 West Main Street, Room 103, Muncie, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The phone is 765-747-7717.

faqs.q: Who can claim surplus from a Delaware County tax sale?
faqs.a: Only the owner whose property was sold. Anyone else must petition the court, even with a power of attorney, and the money is available once a tax deed is issued and recorded.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Delaware County assessment?
faqs.a: June 15 of the year the notice or tax bill is mailed, on Form 130, one petition per parcel. Your notice shows the exact date.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Delaware County house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid taxes and penalties come out of your proceeds at closing, and a cash sale can close before a tax sale happens.
